{{Quote|These are the Taurill, semi-intelligent creatures, busy workers and good pets. They passed all quarantine scans when we arrived on Coruscant. They are insatiably curious and would like to explore. They intend no harm.|Durga the Hutt|<ref name="DS" />}}
'''Taurill''' were small, [[Limb/Legends|multi-limbed]], furry creatures. They scurried about in a way that reminded many [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] beings of vermin. During most of their history, [[Galactic community|the galactic community]] considered the Taurill to be a non-sentient or semi-sentient [[Species/Legends|species]]. However, the Taurill had a [[Hive mind/Legends|hive mind]] controlled by the [[Taurill Overmind]] that gave them full sentience, although an individual Taurill was really only another set of [[Eye/Legends|photoreceptors]] and manipulative organs for the Overmind. When one Taurill noticed something of interest for the Overmind, nearby Taurill ran to analyze that same object from different perspectives, feeding the Overmind with information.

At some point before [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], [[Durga Besadii Tai]], a [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]], came across the Taurill and made a deal with the Overmind. As a result, Durga began to travel in the company of a swarm of his supposed pet Taurill, and he sometimes used them as [[Spy/Legends|spies]] or [[Saboteur/Legends|saboteurs]]. At one point, he even used the Taurill to build a [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]], the [[Darksaber (superweapon)|Darksaber]], but his scheme was a disaster and ended in the [[Death/Legends|death]] of the Hutt and all of the Taurill involved in the project.

==Biology and appearance==
The body of a Taurill was covered in [[Gray (disambiguation)|gray]]-[[Brown (disambiguation)|brown]] fur,<ref name="EGA" /><ref name="DS" /><ref name="ENC">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> except for the tail, the head, and the [[Limb/Legends|limbs]]. The head was shaped like a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Bone/Legends|skull]],<ref name="EGA" /> except for its two constantly-blinking, big, curious<ref name="ENC" /> [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] distanced from the head by [[ommatophora]]. A Taurill had six<ref name="EGA" /><ref name="DS" /> jagged, pointed limbs. Four of those appendages were arms,<ref name="EGA" /><ref name="DS" /><ref name="ENC" /> characterized by their malleability<ref name="DS" /> and their sturdiness. The other two were commonly used as legs, but in certain situations they could be adjusted to be used as a third set of arms,<ref name="EGA" /> as was readily apparent when the Taurill's movements were seen.<ref name="DS" /> Each of the four arms ended in a three-fingered manipulator, while each leg had a pointed, non-fingered end. In addition, a Taurill also had a segmented, arrow-headed tail.<ref name="EGA" />

Taurill were small creatures<ref name="EC" /> that stopped growing once they reached a length of 1.20 [[Meter/Legends|meters]].<ref name="EGA" /> They were flexible enough to squeeze their bodies if needed to explore through very narrow openings.<ref name="DS" /> While the Taurill were [[Primate/Legends|simian]]<ref name="EGA" /> and indeed retained several physical traits of [[Ape/Legends|apes]],<ref name="EC" /> at the same time they also resembled [[Louse/Legends|lice]].<ref name="DS" />

==Society and culture==
While there were thousands of individual Taurill, all of them were controlled by a single collective consciousness, known as the [[Taurill Overmind]], or simply Overmind, to the extent that a Taurill "individual" was only a set of sensory and manipulative organs for a single organism that made up the whole [[Species/Legends|species]].<ref name="EGA" /><ref name="DS" /><ref name="ENC" /> This could also be expressed in a simplified form by saying that Taurill were "eusocial."<ref name="EGA" /><ref name="DS" /><ref name="EC" />

The [[Hive mind/Legends|hive mind]] was interested in gathering information, using the individual Taurill to do so. The Taurill were thus known to look intently in all available directions, as if they were paranoid, to feed information to the Overmind;<ref name="EGA" /> to outsiders, each individual seemed to be trying to gather information for its own interests. The Taurill would swarm over, crawl over, and touch anything or anyone in their range, unless they were met with some resistance.<ref name="DS" /> While in this mode, Taurill would move constantly in a vermin-like way.<ref name="EGA" /><ref name="DS" /><ref name="ENC" /> Taurill were also known to race around.<ref name="AC2">''[[The New Jedi Order: Agents of Chaos II: Jedi Eclipse]]''</ref> At least some individual Taurill had names, as was the case of [[Bortis]].<ref name="HNN">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|47|sports/13314_2.html|Yet Another Greenputt League}}</ref>

Individual Taurill did not have independent thoughts, recognizable emotions, or abstract motivations, leading to the species being classified as semi-[[Sentience/Legends|sentient]].<ref name="EGA" /><ref name="DS" /><ref name="ENC" /> However, considering the hive mind, the Taurill fulfilled the requirements of sentience.<ref name="EC" /> Users of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] scanning the Taurill for intelligence only felt weak, blurred impressions from the collective mind.<ref name="DS" /> As discovered by [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] [[Mammon Hoole]], a Taurill had to be near a collective of other Taurill to receive instructions from the Overmind. Should a Taurill be far enough from the group&mdash;a rare circumstance under normal conditions&mdash;its body would stop moving, as the [[Brain/Legends|brain]] would have stopped to send it any orders. Although the body would remain biologically alive, it would eventually die of hunger or dehydration and would take no independent measure to feed itself.<ref name="EGA" /> When Taurill did eat, their diet included [[shag fern]]s.<ref name="AC1">''[[The New Jedi Order: Agents of Chaos I: Hero's Trial]]''</ref>

==History==
===First contact===
While the origin point of the Taurill was unknown,<ref name="EGA" /> the species was already known&mdash;and labeled non-sentient&mdash;in the later [[Time/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]]. In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the individual Taurill Bortis showed a systematic skill to play the sport known as [[greenputt]] which, along with the discovery of capable [[Neek (creature)|neek]] players, led to the creation of the [[Non-Sentient Professional Greenputt Tour]].<ref name="HNN" />

At some point, a [[Xenobiologist/Legends|xenobiologist]] working as a [[Scout/Legends|scout]] discovered the hive mind of this species while researching in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. This [[Unidentified xenobiologist|individual]] sold this information to [[Durga Besadii Tai]], a young [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]]. Planning to obtain a profit from the Taurill, Durga [[Death/Legends|killed]] the scout to protect the secret, and then approached the Taurill to make a deal. The Hutt offered power and wealth, but the Overmind declined, as it had no need for fortune. The Overmind instead asked Durga to scatter individual Taurill throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], allowing the Overmind to grow. Durga readily accepted and was assigned thousands of Taurill. The Hutt trained the creatures to behave as his pets and to run whenever he clapped his hands.<ref name="DS" /> The creatures proved themselves excellent pets.<ref name="ENC" />

===Stealing the Death Star plans===
[[File:Durga_LoNH.png|thumb|left|Durga the Hutt, who made a deal with the Taurill.]]
In [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], Durga visited [[Chief of State (New Republic)/Legends|Chief of State]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] in [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] as a cover to steal the schemes of the first [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] from the [[Imperial Palace/Legends|Imperial Palace]].<ref name="DS" /><ref name="NGC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> Durga was to be in the company of ninety-eight Taurill that had already received specific instructions of how to behave.<ref name="EGA" /><ref name="EC" /> The creatures, being from an uncommon species, surprised Organa Solo and her companions,<ref name="EGA" /> an effect not repeated by the appearance of Durga's [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]] [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] entourage. When directly asked about the creatures, Durga mentioned that they were harmless,<ref name="DS" /> semi-sentient pets.<ref name="EGA" /><ref name="NGC" /> During the meeting, the Hutt signaled for the Taurill to disperse, claiming that Organa Solo seemed to be distracted by the moving creatures crawling on Durga's body.<ref name="DS" />

Following their orders, two particular Taurill struggled with a guard, trying to seize his ceremonial [[Blaster rifle/Legends|rifle]]. One of the aliens tried to push himself in the barrel while the other "accidentally" pulled the trigger, killing his companion with a resounding blast.<ref name="EGA" /> The guard was astonished at the situation and Durga pretended to be surprised.<ref name="DS" /> The remaining Taurill scattered, apparently scared at the explosion, with some of its fellows hiding in shadows, pieces of furniture, doors or ducts. Durga again pretended to be worried about his pets and ordered the guards to capture all of them.<ref name="EGA" /><ref name="DS" />

The New Republic guards and Organa Solo's [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] began tracking the Taurill, as the Gamorreans proved to be inept for this task. Predictably, this endeavor took several minutes. Meanwhile, three Taurill took advantage of the chaos to reach the [[Imperial Information Center]], in a lower level of the palace, dodging [[Sentry droid/Legends|guard droids]] and accessing a [[computer terminal]]. Using special codes provided by Durga, they accessed secret information, saved it in a small [[Code cylinder/Legends|data cylinder]] and hid it in the fur of one of the creatures.<ref name="DS" /><ref name="NGC" /> The Overmind instantly knew of their success and reported to Durga using another Taurill, one that had been "re-captured" by the Hutt. Durga then ordered one of his assistants to blow an instrument to supposedly soothe the Taurill and summon them.<ref name="EGA" /> Once the Taurill had been gathered, the Gamorreans attempted to count them, but their skills were limited and they required C-3PO's help. Durga attempted to blame Organa Solo for the accident, but she refused to accept culpability and instead accused Durga of bringing uncontrollable pets to [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomatic]] meetings.<ref name="DS" />

===Constructing the Darksaber===
[[File:DarksaberConstruction-TEC.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Taurill building the Darksaber.]]
Soon afterward, C-3PO found Taurill fur in the keyboard the Taurill spy had used. Along with [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], the [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] discovered the crime performed by the Taurill and reported to Organa Solo.<ref name="DS" /> After this, the Chief of State wrote a report explaining the situation and the Taurill incident<ref name="EGA" /> and decided to send a military team to deal with Durga's scheme. Meanwhile, two of Durga's allies, [[General/Legends|General]] [[Sulamar]] and [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Bevel Lemelisk]], used the stolen information to build a new [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] in the safe environment of the [[Hoth asteroid field/Legends|Hoth asteroid field]]. Lemelisk developed the design and trained two individual Taurill to build it, having been told that the whole workforce would get the same knowledge, and provided them with customized [[Environment suit/Legends|space suits]]. As the Taurill worked harder than common sentient workers, Lemelisk estimated that they would build the superweapon faster than any other workforce.<ref name="DS" /> The Taurill began to work as a swarm, following Lemelisk's outlines.<ref name="EC" />

While the Taurill workers appeared to be productive, enthusiastic builders, they were easily distracted: any novelty, such as a nearby moving [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] or visible [[Starship/Legends|starship]], attracted the Overmind's attention, who then sent individual Taurill to catch a new perspective of whatever it was.<ref name="ENC" /> Once the event was over, the individuals took up their jobs again, but they did not return to their intended positions, and as such parts of the Darksaber's construction was incorrect. Because of the species' short attention span, the [[Computer core/Legends|computer core]] was connected to a [[Thermal exhaust port/Legends|thermal exhaust port]], the [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]] anchor points were offset ninety degrees from each other, and several beams were welded to inappropriate places. Lemelisk discovered this disaster but decided to not report it to Durga, as the Hutt could easily blame Lemelisk. Instead, Lemelisk doubled the Taurill shift and supervised them to solve the mistakes. This was achieved in two days.<ref name="DS" />

Soon after, Durga required Lemelisk's presence on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]]. Durga believed the Taurill were performing nicely and Lemelisk could not correct him without risking his wrath.<ref name="DS" /> Thus, Lemelisk told Sulamar about the situation. In Lemelisk's absence, Sulamar worked to keep under control the delays caused by Taurill's short attention span.<ref name="EC" />

[[File:Darksaber.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The Darksaber, built by Taurill]]
The superweapon turned out to be useless due to the Taurill's faulty work and the defective materials used in the construction;<ref name="NGC" /> Lemelisk noted that anyone with a training in technology would have been aware of the weapon's flaws, and only managed to keep a timetable by writing false results. He eventually declared the construction finished, and the Taurill stopped working, instead simply inhabiting the inner rooms of the so-called [[Darksaber (superweapon)|Darksaber]]. Several New Republic agents infiltrated the Darksaber, but one of them, General [[Crix Madine/Legends|Crix Madine]], was captured and taken to Durga at the weapon's [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]]. Durga then executed Madine, with several Taurill intently watching until Lemelisk shooed them away. The Taurill went back to other decks.<ref name="DS" /> Durga, still believing that his Taurill had done a good job, attempted to use the Darksaber to destroy an asteroid. The Darksaber did not work and was destroyed by the collision of two [[Planetoid/Legends|planetoids]] against its frame. Durga died, taking all of the Taurill on board with him.<ref name="EC" /><ref name="DS" /> At some point after the Darksaber episode, Mammon Hoole included an entry on the Taurill in his publication ''[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''.<ref name="EGA" />

==Taurill in the galaxy==
{{Quote|With the confirmation and certification of consistent game-play skills of three Ambrian neeks and a Taurill named Bortis, the Greenputt Governing Council today announced the formation of the Non-Sentient Professional Greenputt Tour (NSPGT).|HoloNetNews report, 22 BBY|<ref name="HNN" />}}
In the times of the Old Republic, the existence of Taurill was known to the general public, as exemplified by Bortis. At that point, the Taurill were believed to be non-sentient.<ref name="HNN" /> Only after Durga discovered the hive mind and made a deal with the Taurill did they have a chance to expand throughout the galaxy as was the Overmind's wish. From that point onward, the Taurill were mostly seen as Durga's personal pets.<ref name="DS" />

The collective mind of the Taurill was an important advantage when trying to create a unified Taurill workforce: the foreman only had to train one Taurill, and all of available Taurill would take advantage of that training.<ref name="EGA" /> Although the Taurill would then work tirelessly, moved by an untiring Overmind,<ref name="DS" /> they were easily distracted, which could lead to spoiled work.<ref name="EC" /> Other limitations included the inability to develop advanced technology themselves, and their strange appearance that could confound the foreman.<ref name="DS" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|While some believe a million monkeys on a million typewriters might some day produce ''Hamlet'', it turns out thousands of simple-minded Taurill workers can't construct a working deep space cannon.|Pablo Hidalgo|<ref name="Checklist">{{SWArchive|url=eu/lit/ref/f20080104/indexp9.html|text=Checklist: 10 ''Star Wars'' Superweapons - Darksaber}}</ref>}}
The Taurill first appeared in the novel [[Darksaber (novel)|''Darksaber'']], written by [[Kevin J. Anderson]], and first published in [[1995]]. The species was first graphically depicted in [[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']] in [[2000]] with an illustration by [[Bill Hughes]].

''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'' unambiguously lists the height of an adult Taurill as 1.20 meters. However, in ''Darksaber'', Leia Organa Solo considers that one of those creatures has the approximate size of her forearm.<ref name="DS" /> ''The Essential Chronology'' provides a picture of the Taurill building the ''Darksaber'' and apparently surviving in a vacuum without the pressure suit Lemelisk provides them in the novel, directly contradicting that story.
